author: Norse Digital Group LLC

sections.faq:
Do I need an API key or an ElevenLabs account?

No. You get 10,000 free welcome credits when you connect your site, and no ElevenLabs account is needed. You can optionally connect your own ElevenLabs API key for an extra 10,000 monthly credits, subject to ElevenLabs’ plan terms: their free plan does not include a commercial licence, so a commercial site needs a paid ElevenLabs plan for that route. Their free plan also requires attribution to ElevenLabs on published content.

What is TTSWP Dashboard?

It is the TTSWP cloud dashboard where you manage your plan, credits, connected sites, and billing. Connect your WordPress site from the plugin’s Overview page with one click.

What is the difference between Free, Pro and Agency?

Free includes 10,000 welcome credits and standard voices in 30+ languages.

Pro Lite is the entry paid plan. It unlocks the PRO feature set, but it includes no TTSWP credits: you connect your own ElevenLabs key and pay ElevenLabs for the speech itself. Audio is stored on your own server rather than on the TTSWP cloud and CDN, and which voices you can use depends on your own ElevenLabs plan.

The credit-inclusive Pro plans start at 50,000 credits per month. They cover the speech cost, add TTSWP cloud storage and CDN delivery, and give access to the full 600+ voice library across 70+ languages without an ElevenLabs account of your own.

Agency adds unlimited sites, white-label branding, credit allocation per site, and dedicated support.

Current plans and prices are at ttswp.com/pricing.

Is the text to speech player accessible?

The audio controls include ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and colour-contrast options, so the player supports your accessibility work. Whether a whole site meets a standard such as WCAG 2.1 AA depends on the rest of the site, not on any single plugin.

Which languages does text to speech support?

Free includes standard voices in 30+ languages. Credit-inclusive Pro and Agency plans unlock 600+ premium voices across 70+ languages. On Pro Lite you get the voices your own ElevenLabs plan allows.

Does text to speech work with Elementor, Divi, or Gutenberg?

It is tested with Elementor, Gutenberg, Divi, Avada, Themify and other popular builders, with specific compatibility fixes for each. If your theme or builder renders content in an unusual way, the CSS Selectors page lets you tell the plugin exactly which elements to read.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. You can generate audio for product descriptions, including title, price, stock status, and category.

Can I bulk-convert existing posts to audio?

Yes. Open My Content & Audio, select the posts you want, and choose Generate selected. It runs one post at a time and stops if your credits run out.

Will text to speech slow down my site?

The player’s scripts and styles are minified and load only on pages that actually have audio, so pages without audio carry no plugin assets at all. The player also works with caching plugins such as WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache and W3 Total Cache.

Can I use my own voice?

Yes. Pro users can enter their custom ElevenLabs Voice ID for voice cloning.

What happens when I run out of credits?

Existing audio stays playable. New audio will not generate until you top up credits, your monthly credits renew, or your ElevenLabs API key fallback kicks in.

Can I manage multiple sites from one account?

Yes. Connect multiple WordPress sites to your TTSWP account. Agency plans include unlimited sites with per-site credit allocation.
sections.changelog:
3.3.33 – 2026-09-25

  • Improved: The plugin sidebar now opens with every menu section expanded except System & Help. Sections you open or close are still remembered.
  • Improved: New installs now show the audio player at full width by default. Existing sites keep their current width setting.
  • Fixed: The Getting Started steps “Customize the audio player” and “Generate your first audio” now show as Done once you have completed them.
  • Fixed: When a site gets no welcome credits because they were already claimed for the same domain, the notice now says so instead of saying your credits are used up.

3.3.32 – 2026-09-22

  • Fixed: Publishing or importing several posts at once could leave most of them without audio, because they all started generating at the same moment. Posts now generate one after another, and a request turned away because the service is busy is retried rather than abandoned.
  • Fixed: Voices your connected ElevenLabs account is not allowed to use can no longer be selected. They now show as unavailable in the picker, with what to do about it, instead of failing at generation time.
  • Fixed: When your credits run out, generation now stops at the first post instead of trying every remaining one, and the notice tells you how many credits the post needed and how many you have.
  • New: The audio box in the post editor shows roughly what generating that post will cost, and how many credits you have, before you generate it. Plans that run on your own ElevenLabs key do not show it, since ElevenLabs bills that generation directly.
  • Security: Your ElevenLabs API key is now handed to the TTSWP service directly between the two servers instead of travelling in the connect link. If you connected your own ElevenLabs key before this version, we recommend creating a new key in ElevenLabs and replacing the old one.
  • Security: Visitor-triggered audio generation now strictly respects the post types you enabled.
  • Fixed: One error message from the player’s recovery script could appear in a visitor’s browser console even with diagnostics turned off. It now follows the same setting as the rest of that script’s output.
  • Security: Imported settings now go through the same validation as settings entered in the plugin’s own screens.
  • Performance: While a visitor waits for audio they triggered, the page checks for the result on a widening interval. It responds sooner at the start and makes less than half as many background requests over a long wait.
  • Performance: Sites using visitor-driven generation no longer accumulate leftover daily counters in the database. Old ones are cleared automatically, keeping the last week.
  • Performance: The audio length used in structured data is worked out once per audio file instead of on every visit to the post.
  • Performance: The player styling used by the audio column is no longer loaded on every screen in the WordPress admin. It now loads only where that column actually appears: the post list and the post editor, for the post types you have enabled.
  • Performance: The voice list the Voices page downloads is about 200 KB smaller, a fifth less than before, after dropping two pieces of voice data the picker never used. Nothing changes in what you see or can filter by.
  • Fixed: Player statistics for a day the site did not run its scheduled job were lost for good. Any day still inside the 30-day window is now caught up on the next run, and the daily summary is much lighter on the database.
  • Security: The TTS language setting is validated before it is used in audio filenames.
  • Security: Tightened the rules for which addresses the plugin will fetch audio from.
  • Security: Audio staged for transcription is stored under an unguessable name, and the plugin’s audio folders can no longer be listed.
  • Security: Dismissing the low-credit notice now requires the same administrator permission as seeing it.
  • Security: Stored ElevenLabs and storage keys now use authenticated encryption, so a tampered value is rejected rather than silently accepted. Existing keys keep working and are upgraded the next time they are saved.

3.3.31 – 2026-09-14

  • Performance: Frontend scripts and styles now ship minified. The player page payload drops from about 300 KB to about 140 KB of plugin JavaScript and CSS. Set SCRIPT_DEBUG to load the readable sources.
  • Performance: The check that decides whether player assets are needed now runs once per page instead of around ten times, and theme compatibility no longer builds a fresh player object for every content filter call.
  • Performance: The transcriptions table is verified with the other plugin tables once a day instead of on every admin page load, the Custom Voice ID lookup runs once per generation instead of once per setting read, and archive pages skip the excerpt detection work that only matters on single posts.
  • Performance: The info popup script is only loaded when the Info control is enabled.
  • Security: Player statistics now validate which posts and fields they accept, and rate-limit each visitor.
  • Security: The Generate on click status endpoint now answers only for posts the button could legitimately appear on.
  • Security: Settings export and import skip license keys, generated audio maps, diagnostics settings and database version stamps, using one shared list for both directions.
  • Security: Hardened the escaping of audio structured data.
  • Developer: Removed about 800 lines of unreachable code, including nine AJAX handlers that no screen called and the unused API key reveal handler.

3.3.30 – 2026-09-08

  • Security: Tightened access control on the shortcode audio generator, which now requires an editor account.
  • Security (PRO): Generate on click and Generate on first visit now reserve each post’s estimated cost against the daily credit cap, and limit how many generations a single visitor can trigger.
  • Security: Password-protected posts keep their player, audio and structured data hidden until the password is entered, and are not offered to visitors for generation.
  • Security: Credential values are masked in the plugin’s debug log lines.
  • Performance: Frontend pages load all plugin settings in one query instead of one query per setting. On sites without an object cache this removes about 36 database queries per page view.
  • Performance: Player statistics no longer run a cache-clearing query on the options table for every tracked event, and the 30-second playback progress events, which were never used in reports, are no longer sent.
  • Performance: The plugin no longer tells WP Rocket to leave jQuery undeferred on every page of the site. Our own scripts wait for jQuery when a cache plugin delays it.
  • Performance: The Overview page reuses the account data it already has instead of making two live requests to the TTSWP service on every view. Add ?refresh=1 to the URL to force a fresh fetch.
  • Performance: Publishing from the classic editor now hands audio generation to the background queue, the same way the block editor already did, instead of holding the publish request until the audio is finished.

3.3.29 – 2026-08-31

  • New (PRO): Generate on click. Posts without audio can show a “Listen to the content” button, so a reader never lands on a page with nothing to play. Clicking it generates the audio on the spot and the page refreshes into the ready player, usually within a minute. It follows your Player Visibility setting, works in every player position, and shares the daily credit cap with Generate on first visit. Turn it on under Content.
  • Improvement: Generating audio now clears that post’s page cache in LiteSpeed Cache, WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, and WP Fastest Cache. Cached sites previously kept serving the page without a player until the cache expired on its own, even though the audio was ready.
  • Improvement: The Content page’s Automatic Audio Generation card was reorganized: publish and first-visit triggers side by side, the new on-click trigger below, and one shared daily credit cap for all visitor-driven generation.

3.3.28 – 2026-08-26

  • New (PRO): Auto-generate on first visit. Let your readers decide what is worth narrating: once a post has been read a few times, its audio is queued in the background, so posts nobody opens never cost you a credit. You set the visit threshold and a daily credit cap. Ideal for large archives, and pages stay fast because audio is never created while a visitor is waiting.
  • Fix: The PRO support request form no longer clears what you typed when a required field is missing.
  • Improvement: The PRO Support page now opens with a short “Before You Report a Bug” checklist that links straight to the debug settings, so the diagnostic log is already recording when you reproduce the problem. This gets most tickets answered in one reply instead of several.
  • Improvement: Free users can now dismiss the PRO upgrade card on the Shortcode Generator page. Dismissing it hides the card for 60 days and gives the text box the full width of the page. The dismissal is remembered per user, so it does not hide the card for your colleagues.
  • Improvement: Design refresh across the plugin admin. Consistent spacing and typography, a single icon set, clearer status colours and better text contrast throughout, for easier reading and improved accessibility.
  • Improvement: The plugin is now shown as “Text to Speech – TTSWP” in the WordPress admin, matching its name on WordPress.org.

Older releases are listed at ttswp.com/docs/changelog.
sections.description:
Text to speech for WordPress with natural ElevenLabs AI voices, an accessible audio player, and 10,000 free credits to start.

Add Text to Speech to WordPress in Seconds

Text to Speech – TTSWP is built for sites that need more than a basic read-aloud button. One plugin covers ElevenLabs voices, speech-to-text, voice cloning, members-only audio, visitor-triggered generation with a daily credit cap, and white-label reselling for agencies.

The plugin is published and operated by Norse Digital Group LLC, a Wyoming-registered company (Sheridan, WY, USA). Engineering work is performed by Mementor Webdesign & Digitalt Markedsføringsbyrå AS, our Norwegian development partner.

The plugin uses ElevenLabs to generate lifelike speech that sounds human, warm and clear, and gives visitors another way to consume your content. PRO and Agency add Speech-to-Text, useful for transcripts, captions, or turning podcasts and video into readable text.

Key Benefits

  • No ElevenLabs account or API key needed. Install, connect your site, and start converting text to speech
  • Natural male, female and multilingual ElevenLabs voices, in a range of tones and styles to match your brand
  • Automatic, mobile-friendly audio player that fits any screen size, with sensible defaults out of the box
  • Accessible player with ARIA labels, keyboard support and colour-contrast options, built to support your WCAG work
  • Tested with Elementor, Gutenberg, Divi, Avada, Themify and other popular builders, and designed to fit alongside common caching, translation and SEO plugins
  • 10,000 free text-to-speech characters when you connect your site, so you can try it at no cost
  • Lazy-loaded and minified assets, loaded only on pages that actually have audio, to keep page weight low
  • AudioObject structured data on every post with audio, so search engines can read the file, its title and its duration (PRO)
  • Speech-to-Text transcription to create written transcripts from your audio content (PRO)

Features

Free Features

  • 10,000 free characters to convert text to audio. Enough to get started without paying
  • Natural male and female voices in multiple languages for a professional listening experience
  • Automatic player for posts, pages, and WooCommerce products with no manual setup needed
  • Flexible player placement – before title, after title, after content, before excerpt, or after excerpt
  • RTL support for languages like Arabic, Hebrew, and Persian so the player displays correctly in right-to-left layouts
  • Quick start. Activate, connect, and the audio player is ready
  • Mobile-first player with speed control and download so visitors can listen anywhere
  • Regenerate audio for a post in one click after you edit it, from the post list or the editor
  • My Content & Audio page, a single hub to generate, regenerate, download, and delete audio for any post, page, or WooCommerce product, one at a time or in bulk, with live credit balance and per-language support
  • Statistics dashboard to track how many visitors listen to your content
  • Shortcode and block support for custom player placement anywhere on your site
  • Content filtering with CSS selectors or no-audio class to exclude specific sections from narration
  • Built for caching and performance plugins like WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, and W3 Total Cache
  • Multisite support for managing text-to-speech across multiple WordPress sites from one network
  • Sticky Footer Player. A persistent audio player bar pinned to the bottom of the page. Visitors can keep reading while listening. Includes play, pause, seek, volume, speed, and close controls
  • Waveform Progress Bar. A visual waveform replaces the standard progress bar. Each post gets a unique pattern. Shows real-time playback progress with accent-colored bars
  • Background Opacity. Adjust the sticky footer’s background transparency so page content shows through while the player stays accessible

PRO & Agency Features

  • 600+ voices across 70+ languages to match your audience worldwide, on credit-inclusive plans
  • Premium 44.1 kHz (192 kbps) audio quality for studio-grade narration
  • ElevenLabs v2 and Eleven v3 models for the latest and most natural-sounding voice technology
  • Speech-to-Text transcription to create written transcripts from audio
  • Voice cloning with ElevenLabs Voice ID to create a custom brand voice
  • Word replacement and pronunciation correction for names, abbreviations, and technical terms
  • SSML support for fine-tuned control over speech output
  • Custom pauses to add natural breaks between sections, headings, or paragraphs
  • AudioObject schema for SEO. Structured data that helps search engines index your audio content
  • Custom intro and outro to add branding or disclaimers to every audio file
  • WPML, GTranslate, and Weglot multi-language voice mapping to assign different voices per language
  • Amazon S3 media offload to reduce server load and speed up audio delivery
  • Audio statistics per post: play clicks, completions, listening time and unique sessions, recorded on your own site
  • White-label mode (Agency plan) to remove plugin branding from the backend and the text-to-speech player
  • White-label the player info tooltip with your own attribution text or agency branding
  • Resell or share our Text-to-Speech plugin (Agency plan) under your own brand and pricing. Offer text-to-speech as a service to your clients and create a recurring revenue stream
  • Credit Allocation per Site (Agency plan). Distribute credits across client sites from one account. Control usage per site to manage costs and ensure fair allocation
  • Priority support with faster response times from the development team
  • Custom audio files. Upload your own audio files.
  • Player Visibility. Show the audio player to everyone, logged-in users only, or selected user roles. Works with membership plugins such as MemberPress, so you can offer audio as a members-only perk across your whole site with no per-post setup
  • Auto-generate on first visit. Let your readers decide what is worth narrating. Once a post has been read a few times, its audio is queued in the background, so the posts nobody opens never cost you a credit. Ideal for large archives. You set the visit threshold and a daily credit cap, and pages stay fast because audio is never created while a visitor is waiting
  • Generate on click. Show a “Listen to the content” button on posts without audio, so a reader never lands on a page with nothing to play. A click generates the audio on demand and the player appears when it is ready. The button follows your Player Visibility setting, which makes it perfect for paid audio subscriptions, and it shares the daily credit cap with Generate on first visit

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin from your WordPress dashboard
  2. Click “Connect Site” on the Overview page. Your 10,000 welcome credits are added at this point
  3. Open a post and click Generate in the Text to Speech box, or turn on automatic generation on publish (PRO)
  4. A text-to-speech audio player appears on the page with no extra configuration
  5. Visitors can play, pause, adjust speed, or download the audio file

Video Walkthrough

Features:
https://ttswp.com/features

Pricing:
https://ttswp.com/pricing

Documentation and setup guides:
https://ttswp.com/docs

Supported Languages

The plugin generates speech in 70+ languages, and its admin screens are translated by the WordPress community at translate.wordpress.org. It works alongside WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress, GTranslate and Weglot, with per-language voice mapping on PRO.

Localised information is available in English and Norwegian.

Use Cases

  • Accessibility and inclusion. Offer an audio version of written content, and help readers with dyslexia, ADHD or visual impairments listen hands-free
  • Blogs and news. Let readers listen to articles while on the go
  • E-commerce product descriptions. Give shoppers the option to hear product details before buying
  • Education. Help students absorb course material through audio learning
  • Long-form content. Turn guides, reports, and documentation into easy-to-consume audio
  • Multitaskers. Serve visitors who prefer listening while commuting, exercising, or working
  • Membership sites. Offer article audio as a members-only perk by showing the player only to logged-in members or selected roles (PRO)
  • Multilingual sites. Reach audiences in their preferred language with per-language voices
  • Content creators. Repurpose written content into audio format without extra recording effort

Other Tools and Plugins

  • Broken Link Checker: WordPress Plugin Page – Check for Broken Links

Standard Installation

  1. Go to Plugins, then Add New, in your WordPress admin
  2. Search for “Text to Speech – TTSWP”
  3. Click Install Now and then Activate
  4. Click “Connect Site” on the Overview page to link your site to TTSWP
  5. You receive 10,000 free welcome credits instantly
  6. Optional: connect your own ElevenLabs API key for 10,000 extra monthly credits, subject to ElevenLabs’ plan terms. Their free plan does not include a commercial licence, so a commercial site needs a paid ElevenLabs plan to use it this way. Their free plan also requires attribution to ElevenLabs on published content
  7. Optional: upgrade to Pro or Agency for more credits and features

Quick Start Guide

  1. Overview – see your plan, credits, and setup checklist at a glance
  2. Voices – pick a default voice and language for your audio
  3. Player – customize colors, size, position, and player label
  4. Content – choose which post types generate audio and set content rules
  5. My Content & Audio – browse, search, and manage all generated audio files
  6. Statistics – track play counts and listener engagement
  7. Shortcode Generator – create custom player embeds for any content
  8. Bulk generation – select multiple posts on My Content & Audio and generate their audio in one run

External Services

ElevenLabs API

Purpose: Converts your text into natural-sounding speech. Speech generation is routed through the TTSWP service below, which calls ElevenLabs on your behalf, so your text never goes to ElevenLabs straight from your site. If you connect your own ElevenLabs key, that key is used for the call instead of ours, and the plugin also contacts ElevenLabs directly from your site to read that account’s own usage and subscription status for display in the admin.
Data sent: The post text you chose to convert, the selected voice and model, the language code, and for Speech-to-Text the audio file to transcribe. On the direct calls described above, your own ElevenLabs API key, sent as a request header so ElevenLabs can identify the account.
When: On manual or automatic audio generation, on Speech-to-Text transcription, and whenever a plugin admin screen shows your ElevenLabs account status, usage or remaining characters.
Storage: MP3 files saved on your own server, or on TTSWP cloud storage (Amazon S3 and CloudFront) on plans that include it.
Limits: The free plan includes 10,000 one-time welcome credits. Paid plans either run on your own ElevenLabs key or include a monthly TTSWP credit allowance. Current plans and prices are at ttswp.com/pricing.
Terms: https://elevenlabs.io/terms-of-use
Privacy: https://elevenlabs.io/privacy-policy

TTSWP Cloud Platform (Norse Digital Group LLC)

Purpose: Generates your audio and handles checkout, subscriptions, and licence validation. All speech generation is routed through this service, which calls ElevenLabs on your behalf.
Data sent: The post text you choose to convert, the selected voice and model, your site’s connection token, and the plugin version. Your own ElevenLabs API key, if you connect one, which the service stores encrypted and uses to call ElevenLabs on your behalf. With Remote Debug Logging enabled, diagnostic events, and with “Include Content Samples” also enabled, text samples from the post being generated. For Speech-to-Text, the address of the audio file to transcribe.
When: When you generate audio or request a transcription, when visitor-triggered generation runs, and when the plugin refreshes your plan and credit balance.
Terms: https://ttswp.com/terms
Privacy: https://ttswp.com/docs/trust/privacy

Amazon Web Services (S3 and CloudFront)

Purpose: Stores and delivers generated audio files for plans that use TTSWP cloud storage. Audio is uploaded to Amazon S3 and served through the Amazon CloudFront CDN.
Data sent: The generated MP3 file. When a visitor plays that audio, their browser requests the file from CloudFront, so their IP address and user agent are visible to AWS in the same way as any CDN-hosted file.
When: On audio generation (upload) and on every playback of cloud-hosted audio (delivery).
Note: Free and Pro Lite plans store audio on your own server instead, so no audio is sent to AWS.
Privacy: https://aws.amazon.com/privacy/

Translations

We’re looking for contributors to help translate this plugin. If you can help, we’d love to hear from you. Contact us and we’ll guide you through the process.

Privacy

No usage analytics or telemetry
This plugin sends no usage data, analytics or telemetry to the plugin author.

Your ElevenLabs API key
If you connect your own ElevenLabs key, it is stored in two places. An encrypted copy stays in your site’s own database, and a copy is held encrypted by the TTSWP service, which uses it server-side to call ElevenLabs when your plan runs on your own key, or as a fallback when your TTSWP credits run out. A key you had already saved in the plugin is sent to the service during Connect Site, directly from your server to ours rather than through your browser, and the local copy is kept, not deleted. Remove the key from your TTSWP account to stop the service using it, and clear it in the plugin settings to remove the local copy.

Player statistics stay on your site
The Player Statistics feature records how your audio is used: play clicks, completions, listening time, and a randomly generated id used to tell one listening session from another. If the visitor is logged in, their WordPress user ID is stored with the event. Those rows are written to tables in your own WordPress database, are shown only to you in the plugin’s Statistics screen, and are never transmitted anywhere. No IP address is stored: a visitor’s address is hashed into a short-lived key purely to rate-limit the endpoint, and it expires after a minute. Statistics are on by default and can be switched off under Settings, which stops collection immediately.

What leaves your site

Every external service the plugin uses, what is sent to each one and when, is listed under External Services above. In short: your text goes out when you generate audio, visitor activity can trigger that generation if you enable the PRO on-visit or on-click features, and cloud-hosted audio is delivered to visitors from Amazon CloudFront. CloudFront access logging is switched off on our distribution, so we keep no log of who played what.

Uninstalling the plugin removes its options, database tables and post meta when full data removal is enabled under Advanced settings. That clears the local copy of your ElevenLabs key, but not the copy held by the TTSWP service: remove that from your TTSWP account if you want it gone.

We never collect:

  • Personal information about your visitors
  • The content of posts you have not chosen to convert
  • Your WordPress password or database credentials

Credits

Natural voice synthesis by ElevenLabs

Published by Norse Digital Group LLC. Engineering by Mementor Webdesign & Digitalt Markedsføringsbyrå AS under contract with Norse Digital Group LLC.

Privacy

No usage analytics or telemetry
This plugin sends no usage data, analytics or telemetry to the plugin author.

Your ElevenLabs API key
If you connect your own ElevenLabs key, it is stored in two places. An encrypted copy stays in your site’s own database, and a copy is held encrypted by the TTSWP service, which uses it server-side to call ElevenLabs when your plan runs on your own key, or as a fallback when your TTSWP credits run out. A key you had already saved in the plugin is sent to the service during Connect Site, directly from your server to ours rather than through your browser, and the local copy is kept, not deleted. Remove the key from your TTSWP account to stop the service using it, and clear it in the plugin settings to remove the local copy.

Player statistics stay on your site
The Player Statistics feature records how your audio is used: play clicks, completions, listening time, and a randomly generated id used to tell one listening session from another. If the visitor is logged in, their WordPress user ID is stored with the event. Those rows are written to tables in your own WordPress database, are shown only to you in the plugin’s Statistics screen, and are never transmitted anywhere. No IP address is stored: a visitor’s address is hashed into a short-lived key purely to rate-limit the endpoint, and it expires after a minute. Statistics are on by default and can be switched off under Settings, which stops collection immediately.

What leaves your site

Every external service the plugin uses, what is sent to each one and when, is listed under External Services above. In short: your text goes out when you generate audio, visitor activity can trigger that generation if you enable the PRO on-visit or on-click features, and cloud-hosted audio is delivered to visitors from Amazon CloudFront. CloudFront access logging is switched off on our distribution, so we keep no log of who played what.

Uninstalling the plugin removes its options, database tables and post meta when full data removal is enabled under Advanced settings. That clears the local copy of your ElevenLabs key, but not the copy held by the TTSWP service: remove that from your TTSWP account if you want it gone.

We never collect:

  • Personal information about your visitors
  • The content of posts you have not chosen to convert
  • Your WordPress password or database credentials
